sentences.show: The rocket that led to the Moon began as a Nazi weapon, built by prisoners.
Its first successful flight was on this day in 1942.
The V-2 climbed 84.5 kilometres into the sky.
Its commander, Walter Dornberger, called it the first day of a new era: space travel.
Hitler saw something else. A weapon of vengeance.
It was built in tunnels, by concentration camp prisoners.
From September 1944, more than 3,000 were fired, first at London, then Antwerp and Liège.
It fell faster than sound. There was no warning.
In London alone, it killed about 2,700 people.
Yet more people died building it than were killed by it.
After the war, its designer, Wernher von Braun, surrendered to the Americans.
In America, he became chief architect of the Saturn V.
The rocket that carried Apollo to the Moon.
